content.title: About
content.content: Ham croquette is a bite‑size fried snack made from minced ham, breadcrumbs, eggs and seasonings. It has a golden, crunchy crust and a tender, flavorful interior. The product is ready to eat after heating and works well as an appetizer, side dish or fast‑food component.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Croquettes originated in Europe in the 19th century as a way to use leftover meat.
The ham used is often smoked, giving the croquette its distinctive aroma.
Traditionally croquettes are hand‑shaped, but industrial production uses molding machines.
They are commonly served with sauces such as mustard, creamy or tomato‑based sauces.
In some countries ham croquettes are sold as a popular street‑food snack.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Ham provides high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron from meat supports oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Ham supplies vitamin B12 and niacin, which help nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Energy provision
items.content: Croquettes deliver quick energy through a balance of protein, fat and carbohydrates.

items.title: Zinc content
items.content: Zinc contributes to immune response and wound healing.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Ham is often salty, so people with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Croquettes can contain notable amounts of saturated fat, which should be moderated.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have an allergy or intolerance to pork.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Industrial croquettes may contain nitrites and other preservatives that some consumers avoid.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat ham croquettes in an oven, microwave or skillet until the crust is golden. Serve hot with mustard, creamy or tomato sauce, and pair with vegetable sides.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep croquettes in the original packaging in the refrigerator at 0 °C to +4 °C. Once opened, consume within 3‑5 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag at –18 °C and reheat thoroughly before eating.
